items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So I got Les Hite's band and my band and put them together.

ctx.x: No, just march. But previous to that they always had marching bands. So I made a proposition with the black union out there -- they had a black union and white union. I said, well, why don't we put together a gigantic swing band and blow in this parade. They said, how you going to do it? I said, well, let me handle it.

So I got Les Hite's band and my band and put them together. Had ten saxophones, ten brass, used four guitar players and two tuba players. And I made an arrangement on "Swing High, Swing Low," and one on "Christopher Columbus." And we rehearsed for two weeks and we went into this parade.
